newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian students call for election boycott.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian students call for election boycott.

text.p: About 100 students backing the ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Megawati Sukarnoputri, demonstrated in front of parliament on Thursday to call for a boycott of May 29 elections.
No arrests were reported and the students dispersed after one of them read a petition. "We reject the 1997 election which does not involve the PDI under Megawati Sukarnoputri," the petition said.
Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, was ousted as PDI leader at a government-backed congress last June which elected deputy House speaker Surjadi.

The government has rejected the list of candidates for the next parliament drawn up by Megawati, who says she is still the legitimate PDI leader. The government instead recognised the candidate list made by Surjadi.
Megawati has so far made no call for a poll boycott.
The students also demanded the release of sacked legislator Sri Bintang Pamungkas, who was arrested last month on charges of subversion for urging Indonesians to boycott the election.
President Suharto said last month authorities would take action against people who encouraged others not to vote in the elections.
Authorities in the university town of Yogyakarta broke up a student demonstration this week after its leaders made calls for an election boycott because of Megawati's exclusion from the poll.

The Kompas newspaper on Thursday quoted the Yogyakarta army commander, Colonel A.R. Gaffar, as saying those who were shown to have called for a poll boycott would be taken to court. He said 24 students were detained after the protest.
Members of the left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD), which is not officially recognised, has started a graffiti campaign calling for a boycott.
Most leaders of the small group, which went underground after being blamed for riots in Jakarta last July, are on trial for subversion, which carries a maximum penalty of death.
Gaffar accused the Yogyakarta protest of being organised by the PRD.
Only three political parties are allowed to contest the general elections -- the PDI, the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and the ruling Golkar.
